summary: Admit a provider-neutral marketplace listing workspace with versioned taxonomy, typed content, bounded batch evidence and explicit live connector qualification gates.

impacts.evidence: Taxonomy evidence, previews and batch journals carry authenticated organization/workspace scope and repository reads use forced tenant RLS.
Listing records retain bounded drafts, references, digests and diagnostics while excluding credentials, raw provider payloads and unnecessary customer data.
Taxonomy, preview, apply, batch and read-after-write routes are additive OpenAPI contracts with generated Go, Python and TypeScript clients.
The batch journal is an immutable command boundary; future asynchronous transitions must use the canonical versioned envelope and transactional outbox.
Listing taxonomy, write and status operations are typed connector ports and capabilities, with provider differences kept outside Core.
Migration 52 adds bounded taxonomy and batch evidence tables with backup metadata, forced RLS, tenant policies and immutable triggers.
Released media references, safe error responses, approval binding and explicit live qualification keep untrusted assets and remote writes fail-closed.
Batch apply requires an authenticated idempotency key and an approved action bound to the exact preview, while MCP is preview-only.
Preview and batch records preserve input digests, taxonomy fingerprints, before/after row digests, approval reference and immutable timestamps.
Stable preview and batch identifiers, idempotent persistence and typed read-after-write drift handling cover duplicate, mismatch and unknown outcomes.
The repository slice has no caller-controlled remote destination; live provider transport remains behind fixed connector boundaries and qualification evidence.
The operator surface exposes bounded batch counts, row diagnostics, state and reconciliation decisions without exposing secrets or raw remote responses.
Batch evidence is append-only, live capability admission can be disabled, and the expand-only migration has no destructive rollback path.
Core, API, persistence, migration, contract, generated SDK, frontend and synthetic 1,000-SKU qualification checks cover the repository boundary; live credentials remain a release gate.
